note: All figures are FACT, transcribed from Novartis results releases in sources.json/signals.json. Interpretations are labeled ai_hypothesis and separated from fact.

fact.capital_return: Dividend CHF 3.70/share (+5.7%, 29th consecutive increase); $8.9bn repurchased in 2025 plus a new $10bn buyback authorization.

quarters.ai_hypothesis: A 40.1% core margin delivered two years ahead of plan plus sustained capital returns signals management confidence that pipeline and priority-brand growth will offset patent-cliff losses, keeping commercial budgets intact.

fact.driver_note: US generic erosion (notably Entresto) outweighed priority-brand growth.

quarters.ai_hypothesis: The Q1 dip quantifies how sharply loss of exclusivity bites before launches compound, underscoring the urgency of faster new-brand uptake.

fact.brand_highlights: Kisqali $1.695bn (+43%); Cosentyx $1.824bn (+10%); Kesimpta $1.424bn (+32%); Scemblix $562M (+89%); Pluvicto $651M (+43%); Leqvio $480M (+59%).
fact.erosion_note: Entresto $1.181bn, -51% cc on US generic competition.

quarters.ai_hypothesis: A return to top-line growth after Q1's decline suggests priority-brand momentum is beginning to outpace generic erosion, but the -19% net income shows launch, integration and financing costs pressuring the P&L and sharpening ROI scrutiny.

fact.long_term_2025_2030_cagr: +5-6% cc sales CAGR; return to 40%+ core margin by 2029; 30+ potential high-value pipeline assets
fact.context_note: 2026 framed by leadership as the largest patent expiry in Novartis history, to be grown through.

guidance.ai_hypothesis: Guiding to sales growth while core operating income declines in cc reflects the peak-LoE year: launch investment and integration costs weigh on profit even as priority brands lift the top line — raising the premium on cost-efficient, measurable commercialization.
